body:
The current vcpkg master baseline `414b5330a184ea5fbc6ca29f7960b189f6b0392f` contains benchmark 1.9.5, while google/benchmark has released v1.10.0.

Reproduction:

```json
{
  "name": "benchmark-version-repro",
  "version-string": "0.1.0",
  "builtin-baseline": "414b5330a184ea5fbc6ca29f7960b189f6b0392f",
  "dependencies": ["benchmark"]
}
```

Resolving this manifest selects 1.9.5. The upstream release is https://github.com/google/benchmark/releases/tag/v1.10.0 .

Would you update the benchmark port and version database to 1.10.0, including its source hash and platform checks? In link-foundation/links-notation#406 we update the archived template to the current official baseline and document the registry lag, retaining the supported port rather than introducing an unreviewed local overlay.

comments.body:
The newer baseline `4702e381dbbd9b54d3f7e1eb565cd8981c1814cd` still selects Benchmark 1.9.5. Additional build evidence: the existing official port, with only its version and source SHA512 changed to 1.10.0, installs successfully on Linux x64 alongside gtest 1.18.0. The upstream archive SHA512 is `2e024135fb814b888d2232105e0417b38ca555169ae17aa16c714d7de8bb30211ea2b0ff109eb4e04ff2a04de35b4f26e2c18c0cb39e23c8739af7512d3bcd427`.

Tested overlay and build log: https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/pull/31 . We use this overlay temporarily to keep Conan, FetchContent and vcpkg on 1.10.0; an official port/version database update would remove that duplication.

A separate portfile correctness issue surfaced while testing the 1.10.0 overlay copied from baseline `4702e381dbbd9b54d3f7e1eb565cd8981c1814cd` (the same logic is in the current 1.9.5 port):

`vcpkg_check_features(OUT_FEATURE_OPTIONS FEATURE_OPTIONS ...)` produces `-DBENCHMARK_INSTALL_TOOLS=OFF/ON`, but `vcpkg_cmake_configure` receives `${FEATURES}` instead. Those are port feature names (`core`, `tools`), not CMake definitions. Consequently the default/core-only install leaves upstream's default `BENCHMARK_INSTALL_TOOLS=ON`; tools are installed even when the tools feature is omitted.

Minimal reproduction with the current port:

```sh
VCPKG_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1 vcpkg install benchmark:x64-linux --classic --x-install-root=./installed-core-probe
rg BENCHMARK_INSTALL_TOOLS buildtrees/benchmark/x64-linux-rel/CMakeCache.txt
```

Expected: `BENCHMARK_INSTALL_TOOLS:BOOL=OFF`; observed before the correction: `ON`. A tools-enabled install should still set `ON` and relocate its scripts as before. No stress input or extra test dependency is needed.

Suggested code change in `ports/benchmark/portfile.cmake`:

```diff
-        ${FEATURES}
+        ${FEATURE_OPTIONS}
```

The downstream overlay keeps this one-line correction until an upstream port release. PR https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/pull/31 includes a small CMake boundary regression (`test_benchmark_overlay_forwards_feature_options`) that fails on the copied port and checks both ON and OFF on the correction; its native build logs are retained under `dev/log/issues/30/pulls/31/raw/`. This feature forwarding correction is independent of the version/hash update above.

title: [benchmark] Update port from 1.9.5 to upstream 1.10.0
